mainTopic: פיגול when the service or the intent covers only part of the מתירין: the יום כיפור blood, carrying the קומץ, and burning in tiny amounts
overview: First the גמרא admits it has no answer to a wording problem in a ברייתא about the יום כיפור blood. It then asks how רבי מאיר can give כרת for פיגול there, since once the blood is disqualified, the later placements should be like plain water. רבה answers that new animals were brought for each stage. רבא answers that for פיגול, even disqualified placements count. Next it settles three different counts of the יום כיפור blood placements (43, 47 and 48) by tying each count to a different opinion. Then רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether פיגול intent while carrying only the קומץ is like scooping or like burning. רבא explains רבי יוחנן's view, and he defends it against challenges from אביי and רב שימי with the rule that making something holy counts like permitting. A ברייתא that seemed to support רבי יוחנן is pushed aside, and ריש לקיש's reading is left with one unanswered difficulty. Finally, three אמוראים argue about burning the קומץ one sesame seed at a time: פיגול, פסול or כשר. The גמרא shows that each view rests on whether small portions count as eating and as burning, not on an older dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: The 'whether... whether' wording challenges רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא's wording 'whether... whether' goes against רב אשי's narrow reading, and the גמרא admits it is a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the בריתא teaches 'whether... whether'! This is indeed a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the בריתא's wording does not fit רב אשי's explanation. It then admits this is a real problem that it cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא lists each set of blood placements with the word 'whether'. That suggests the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר in all of these cases, not only in the limited case רב אשי described. The one-word reply 'קשיא' means the question stands without an answer, but it does not knock down the whole discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether... whether: a list that covers every case equally
It (the בריתא) teaches
It is a difficulty: the question is left unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end is not a full refutation (תיובתא). It only means the גמרא has no answer right now.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'whether... whether'!
phrases.notes: This is short for the בריתא's list: 'whether in the first set, whether in the second set...'

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge against רב אשי's reading from the earlier discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's narrow reading of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'whether... whether' wording treats all the cases the same, so the dispute cannot be limited to one case.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר's ruling from the בריתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the בריתא and quotes רבי מאיר: the offering is פיגול and one is liable to כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי מאיר says it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the בריתא and quotes רבי מאיר's ruling. This sets up a new question about that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling comes from the case of the יום כיפור blood, where the כהן had a פיגול thought during one set of placements. רבי מאיר says that thought makes the offering פיגול, with the full punishment of כרת for eating it. The next steps will question how כרת is possible here.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering disqualified by an improper intent about when it will be eaten or offered
Spiritual cutting off: the punishment for eating פיגול
One is liable for it

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Meir says: it is piggul,
and one is liable to karet for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר פִּגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of questioning on the בריתא itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a פיגול thought in any one set of placements makes the offering פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: No כרת until all the מתירין are offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states a basic rule: there is no כרת for פיגול unless all the parts of the service that make the offering permitted were completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now consider: one is not liable to כרת unless all the permitting factors have been offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays down a known rule. It is setting up a challenge against רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering only becomes פיגול once its service has been fully completed, including every required blood placement. The word מכדי signals that the גמרא is building toward a question from an accepted principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Now consider: introduces an agreed-upon point that will lead to a question
Permitting factors: the services, such as the blood placements, that make the offering permitted
That they are offered

phrases.english: Now consider: one is not liable to karet
until all the permitting factors have been offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in a general rule to test רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no כרת for פיגול unless all the מתירין were offered.

steps.title: The source: the word יֵרָצֶה
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ירצה' teaches that a disqualified offering is compared to a valid one. Just as a valid offering is accepted only after all the מתירין, an offering only becomes פיגול after all the מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: 'It shall be accepted.' The acceptance of a disqualified offering is like the acceptance of a valid one. Just as a valid offering is accepted only once all the permitting factors are offered, so too a disqualified offering becomes פיגול only once all the permitting factors are offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source in the פסוק for the rule it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about פיגול uses the same word, 'ירצה', that is used for a valid offering. This teaches that the two work the same way. A valid offering only 'works' when the service is complete, so a פיגול offering is also only 'fully' פיגול when the service is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall be accepted
Acceptance: the offering taking effect
Valid
Disqualified

phrases.english: As the Master said:
'It shall be accepted':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18

phrases.english: like the acceptance of a valid offering, so is the acceptance of a disqualified one;
just as the acceptance of a valid offering
is not until all the permitting factors have been offered,
so too the acceptance of a disqualified offering
is not until all the permitting factors have been offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the rule in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that there is no כרת for פיגול until all the מתירין are offered
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'ירצה', which compares a disqualified offering to a valid one

steps.title: Sprinkling in the היכל is like sprinkling water
steps.stepSummary: Once the כהן's פיגול thought inside disqualified the blood, his later sprinklings in the היכל do not count. So the מתירין were never completed, and there should be no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in this case, since he had a פיגול thought about it inside, he disqualified it. When he later sprinkles in the היכל, he is just sprinkling plain water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the challenge against רבי מאיר. It applies the rule from steps 3 and 4 to the יום כיפור case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פיגול thought during the placements inside the קודש הקדשים already disqualified the blood. Any blood placed afterward is not real offering blood, so it is 'just water'. Without a valid completion of all the מתירין, how can רבי מאיר rule that there is כרת?

keyTerms.meaning: He had intent: thought an improper thought
Inside: in the קודש הקדשים
The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים
He sprinkles
Just plain water

steps.whatToRemember: The question: a disqualified service cannot count toward completing the מתירין. So if the פיגול thought came early in the Yom Kippur service, how can there be כרת?

phrases.english: And this one: since he had intent about it inside,
phrases.notes: He means during the first placements, in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: he disqualified it,
so when he sprinkles in the Sanctuary,
it is merely water that he is sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from steps 3 and 4 against רבי מאיר's ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling of פיגול with כרת when the thought came during an early set of placements
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the blood is disqualified, the later placements do not count, so the מתירין were never completed and כרת should not apply.

steps.title: רבה: Four Bulls and Four Goats
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers the difficulty by describing a case where new animals were brought for each stage of the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: You can find this case when there were four bulls and four goats.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question from step 5. He says the ברייתא is talking about a case where a fresh bull and goat were brought for each stage of the יום כיפור blood service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that once the blood became פסול, the later placements should not count, so the מתירין were never finished. רבה says each time the blood spilled after a פיגול thought, new animals were brought for the next stage. So every stage was done with fresh blood, and the whole set of מתירין really was finished.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it; a case where this ruling works
Bulls; here, the כהן גדול's bull of יום כיפור
Goats; here, the goat offered inside on יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying there were four separate יום כיפור services. It is one service, but each stage was finished using blood from a new pair of animals.

phrases.english: Rabba said: You can find it
phrases.notes: He means: you can find a case where the ברייתא's ruling of כרת works.

phrases.english: with four bulls and four goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one bull and one goat, the spoiled blood would mean the מתירין were never completed.
steps.terutzMaskana: With fresh animals for each stage, all the מתירין were truly completed, so כרת applies.

steps.title: רבא: For פיגול, Spoiled Placements Still Count
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that even with one bull and one goat, the later placements count as finishing the מתירין for פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it was one bull and one goat, because for making something פיגול, these placements count as if they were accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same question. He says no new animals are needed: for the rules of פיגול, the later placements still count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed that spoiled blood cannot complete the מתירין. רבא disagrees: in the area of פיגול, finishing the service with that blood counts as completing the מתירין, even though the blood was already disqualified. So the case can be one bull and one goat, and כרת still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say; the case does not need to be narrowed
For making the offering פיגול
They are accepted; they count as a completed service

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. רבה: new animals for each stage. רבא: for פיגול, even spoiled placements count as finishing the מתירין.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer sets a general idea: being 'accepted' for פיגול is not the same as being accepted for כפרה.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא פַּר אֶחָד וְשָׂעִיר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: You can even say it was one bull and one goat,
for making it פיגול, they are accepted.
phrases.notes: He means: the later placements count as finishing the service, but only for the rules of פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 5's קשיא. It does not narrow the case as רבה did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the rule: placements that do not work for כפרה still count for פיגול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Placements made with disqualified blood count for nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For פיגול they count as completing the מתירין, so even one bull and one goat bring כרת.

steps.title: Forty-Three or Forty-Seven Placements?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our ברייתא counts 43 placements, but another ברייתא counts 47.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our ברייתא said forty-three. But another ברייתא teaches forty-seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail of the ברייתא: the number of blood placements on יום כיפור. It shows that another ברייתא gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא counted 43 placements of the bull's and goat's blood. Another ברייתא says 47. Both are describing the same service, so the numbers seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty-three; the count of blood placements in our ברייתא
Forty-seven; the count in another ברייתא

phrases.english: Forty-three,
phrases.notes: This quotes our ברייתא's total number of יום כיפור blood placements.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: forty-seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פיגול question and turns to a different detail of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give different totals for the same service.

steps.title: It Depends on Mixing the Blood for the Corners
steps.stepSummary: The two counts follow two opinions about whether the bull's and goat's blood are mixed before being placed on the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows the opinion that they mix the blood for the corners, and that one follows the opinion that they do not mix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. Each number matches a different opinion about how the corners of the golden מזבח are done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bull's and goat's blood are mixed before going on the four corners, there are 4 placements there, which gives 43. If they are not mixed, the כהן places each animal's blood on the four corners separately. That adds 4 more placements, which gives 47.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
Following the one who says; matching a known opinion
They mix the bull's and goat's blood together
The corners of the golden מזבח

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
this follows the one who says: they mix for the corners,
phrases.notes: 'This' is our ברייתא with 43. Mixing means one set of four placements on the corners.

phrases.english: and that follows the one who says: they do not mix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות describe the same service, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each follows a different opinion about mixing the blood for the corners.

steps.title: A Third Count: Forty-Eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings yet another ברייתא that counts 48 placements.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: forty-eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another contradiction: a third ברייתא gives yet another number, 48.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the 47-count, the highest so far, does not reach 48. So something extra must be counted in this third ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty-eight; the count in a third ברייתא

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: forty-eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up contradiction after step 9's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A third ברייתא counts one more placement than the highest count so far.

steps.title: It Depends on Whether the Leftover Blood Is Required
steps.stepSummary: The 48 count includes pouring out the leftover blood, following the opinion that this pouring is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This follows the one who says the leftover blood is required, and that follows the one who says the leftover blood is not required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the extra one. It depends on whether pouring out the leftover blood is a required part of the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pouring out the leftover blood (שירים) is required, it counts as one more act, which brings the total to 48. If it is not required, it is not counted, and the total stays at 47.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood, poured out after the main placements
They are required; without them the service is not valid

steps.whatToRemember: The three counts come from two disagreements. Mixing for the corners: 43 vs 47. Counting the leftover blood as required: 47 vs 48.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
this follows the one who says: the leftover blood is required,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the 48 count. Since pouring the leftover blood is required, it is counted as one more act.

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: שִׁירַיִם לֹא מְעַכְּבִין.
phrases.english: that follows the one who says: the leftover blood is not required.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: שִׁירַיִם מְעַכְּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 47 and 48 counts contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 48 count treats pouring the leftover blood as required, so it is counted. The 47 count does not.

steps.title: What if the improper intent was during carrying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new question: what happens if someone had פיגול intent only while carrying the קומץ to the מזבח?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he made the offering פיגול during the carrying, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question about the step of carrying (הולכה) the קומץ to the מזבח. This sets up a disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that intent during the burning of only the קומץ, without the לבונה, does not make the offering פיגול. The לבונה is also carried to the מזבח. So the question is whether carrying acts like burning, where both must be included, or whether it is different.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the חכמים (an open question)
He had the forbidden intent that makes an offering פיגול
Carrying the קומץ (or blood) to the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about carrying in general. It is about having the bad intent while carrying only the קומץ, not the לבונה.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
If he had intent of פיגול during the carrying, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Carrying the קומץ to the מזבח, without the same intent while carrying the לבונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of counting blood placements and starts a new question tied to the משנה about פיגול in only part of the מתירין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does פיגול intent while carrying only the קומץ (and not the לבונה) make the מנחה פיגול?

steps.title: Two views: carrying is like scooping, or like burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן compares carrying to קמיצה (so it is פיגול). ריש לקיש compares it to הקטרה (so it is not).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: carrying is like scooping. ריש לקיש said: carrying is like burning.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways. Each one compares carrying to a different step whose law we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קמיצה is done only with the קומץ, so intent during it is enough to make the offering פיגול. הקטרה is done with both the קומץ and the לבונה, so intent with only one of them is not enough. רבי יוחנן puts carrying in the first group, and ריש לקיש puts it in the second.

keyTerms.meaning: Scooping a handful of flour out of the מנחה
Burning on the מזבח
The handful scooped from the מנחה

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: carrying is like scooping,
and ריש לקיש said: carrying is like burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: intent during carrying only the קומץ makes it פיגול (like קמיצה). ריש לקיש: it does not, because it is like הקטרה, where both the קומץ and the לבונה are needed.

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש makes sense because the לבונה is also carried, but why does רבי יוחנן treat carrying like scooping?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for ריש לקיש, because there is also the carrying of the לבונה. But for רבי יוחנן, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says ריש לקיש's view is easy to understand, and then challenges רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לבונה is carried to the מזבח just like the קומץ. So carrying looks like burning, which is done to both of them, and intent with only the קומץ should be only half. Why then does רבי יוחנן say this half is enough to make it פיגול?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one view)... (sets up a contrast with the other view)
Frankincense, burned along with the קומץ
What is the reason?

phrases.english: It makes sense according to ריש לקיש,
since there is also the carrying of the frankincense,
but according to רבי יוחנן, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of רבי יוחנן from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that carrying is like קמיצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לבונה is carried too, so intent during only the קומץ's carrying covers only part of the מתירין. That should not make it פיגול, just like burning only the קומץ.

steps.title: רבא: a step that doesn't permit counts on its own
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יוחנן holds any step that does not itself permit the offering is important enough to cause פיגול by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוחנן holds that any service that does not permit the offering is an important service, so it can make the offering פיגול on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by giving the rule that רבי יוחנן is using.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that you need intent on all the מתירין applies to the step that actually permits the offering, which is the burning. Carrying does not permit anything, so it is not split into halves. Carrying the קומץ is judged as a full, important step by itself, and intent during it makes the offering פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A service step that does not itself permit the offering
An important (significant) service
By itself, on its own
The parts whose offering permits the קרבן (here, the קומץ and the לבונה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: intent during carrying only the קומץ makes the offering פיגול, because a step that does not permit counts on its own. ריש לקיש: carrying is like burning, so both the קומץ and the לבונה are needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic difference between the step that permits the offering (burning), where intent must cover all the מתירין, and the other steps, which count on their own.

phrases.english: רבא said: רבי יוחנן holds:
any service that does not permit the offering,
is an important service
to make the offering פיגול through it by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by explaining רבי יוחנן's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the principle behind the view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Carrying is done to both the קומץ and the לבונה, so intent on only one should be just half, like burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the permitting step (burning) needs intent on all the מתירין. A non-permitting step like carrying is important on its own, so intent during it with the קומץ alone makes the offering פיגול.

steps.title: אביי points to the slaughter of one lamb
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: slaughtering one of the two lambs also does not permit the offering, yet the חכמים still argue and say it cannot make פיגול by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: But look at the slaughter of one of the lambs. That is a service that does not permit the offering, and yet they disagree about it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's rule from step 15 with a case that seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a service that does not permit the offering can cause פיגול by itself. Slaughtering one of the two שבועות lambs does not permit anything, so by that rule it should cause פיגול alone. But there is a מחלוקת about it, and the חכמים say it does not, so the rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs. Here, the two lambs brought together with the שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם on שבועות.
A service that does not itself make the offering permitted.
They disagree.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who gave the explanation in the step before.

phrases.english: But there is the slaughter of one of the lambs,
which is a service that does not permit it,
and yet they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵי שְׁחִיטַת אֶחָד מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that any service that does not permit the offering can cause פיגול by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering one lamb permits nothing, yet the חכמים say it cannot cause כרת alone, so not every non-permitting service is that important.

steps.title: The משנה about the lambs and the frankincense bowls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that backs up אביי: רבי מאיר says one lamb or one bowl of frankincense can cause פיגול, and the חכמים say there is no כרת unless the intent is in the whole permitting factor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he slaughtered one of the lambs intending to eat the two loaves tomorrow, or burned one of the frankincense bowls intending to eat the two rows of showbread tomorrow, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and one is liable to כרת for it. The חכמים say there is no כרת unless he has פיגול intent during the entire permitting factor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for אביי's words "and they disagree."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lambs together permit the שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, and the two בזיכין together permit the לחם הפנים. Each half alone permits nothing. רבי מאיר says bad intent in one half is enough for פיגול. The חכמים require the bad intent during the whole מתיר, which seems to go against רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves, the שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם of שבועות.
The two bowls of frankincense placed with the לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים and burned to permit it.
Rows or arrangements. The two stacks of the לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
Being cut off. The punishment for eating פיגול.
The permitting factor: the service that makes the offering allowed to eat.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
If he slaughtered one of the lambs
intending to eat the two loaves tomorrow,
or burned one of the bowls of frankincense
intending to eat the two rows of bread tomorrow,
Rabbi Meir says:
it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it,
and the Rabbis say: there is no karet for it
unless he has piggul intent during the entire permitting factor.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: שָׁחַט אֶחָד מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים לֶאֱכוֹל שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for אביי's challenge in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים argue about slaughtering one lamb even though it does not permit anything.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about one lamb or one בזך offered with פיגול intent.

steps.title: Slaughtering the lambs makes the loaves holy
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the loaves are not holy from the oven. The slaughter of the lambs makes them holy, and making holy counts like permitting, so each lamb is really half of a מתיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Do you think the bread is already holy in the oven? It is the slaughter of the lambs that makes it holy, and something that comes to make holy is treated like something that comes to permit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his rule. He shows that the slaughter of one lamb is actually part of a permitting step, so it is not a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the loaves were already holy and that only the blood permits them, so the slaughter would be a non-permitting step. רבא says the slaughter is what makes the loaves holy, and that counts as permitting. That makes each lamb half of a מתיר, and half a מתיר cannot cause פיגול alone, so the חכמים fit his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven.
Makes it holy (sanctifies it).
Something that comes to make holy is treated like something that comes to permit.

steps.whatToRemember: Slaughtering the שבועות lambs makes the loaves holy, and making holy counts like permitting. So each lamb is half a מתיר, not an independent non-permitting step.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבא is answering אביי.

phrases.english: Do you think the bread becomes holy in the oven?
The slaughter of the lambs makes it holy,
and what comes to make holy is like what comes to permit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the slaughter is a sanctifying act, which counts as permitting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loaves are holy from the oven, so slaughtering one lamb is a non-permitting step, and the חכמים disagree with רבא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaughter makes the loaves holy, so each lamb is half a מתיר and cannot cause פיגול alone. The חכמים do not contradict רבא's rule.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי brings the ruling of אחרים on the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי begins a new objection from a ברייתא: אחרים rule that if intent for circumcised people came before intent for uncircumcised people the פסח is valid, but in the reverse order it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי raised an objection: אחרים say: If he put the circumcised before the uncircumcised, it is valid. If he put the uncircumcised before the circumcised, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי quotes a ברייתא to set up a new challenge. The exact point of the challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is slaughtering a קרבן פסח, where the two cuts of שחיטה are done with different intents: one for people allowed to eat it (circumcised) and one for people who are not (uncircumcised). אחרים say the order matters. That suggests a single part of the שחיטה can count by itself, and the גמרא will use this to challenge what was just said.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcised people, who may eat the קרבן פסח.
Uncircumcised people, who may not eat the קרבן פסח.
He put first. Here, his intent for one group came first.
Valid / invalid.

steps.confusionAlert: The case is about the קרבן פסח, not a מנחה. It is brought only to compare how one part of a service can count by itself.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi raised an objection:
Acherim say:
If he put the circumcised before the uncircumcised, it is valid;
phrases.notes: He means his intent for circumcised eaters came during the first cut of the שחיטה, and his intent for uncircumcised eaters during the second.

phrases.english: if he put the uncircumcised before the circumcised, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new objection after רבא's answer in step 18, using a ברייתא about the קרבן פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The discussion of whether a partial step of a service can count by itself (רבא's approach).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The objection is being set up here. אחרים let the first part of the שחיטה decide the outcome, and the point of the challenge comes next.

steps.title: רב שימי finishes: they argue about half a permitting factor
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי completes his challenge. The תנא קמא and אחרים argue about חצי מתיר even in the פסח, where the slaughter does not seem to make anything holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that they argue about half of a permitting factor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי finishes the challenge he began in Step 19. He says the ברייתא about the פסח is a case of half a מתיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסח, cutting one of the two סימנים is only half of the slaughter, so it is half a מתיר. Slaughtering a פסח does not seem to make anything else holy, the way the lambs make the loaves holy. Even so, the תנא קמא and אחרים still argue about it, and that clashes with רבא's answer in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us
Half of a permitting factor, such as one of two required parts
They argue

phrases.english: And we hold
that they argue about half of a permitting factor.
phrases.notes: "They" means the תנא קמא and אחרים from the ברייתא about the פסח in Step 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule from step 15, as defended in step 18: a service that does not permit the offering can cause פיגול by itself. A service only splits into halves of a מתיר if it permits, or if it makes something holy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The slaughter of the פסח does not permit anything, since the blood sprinkling does that. It also seems to make nothing holy. By רבא's rule, cutting one סימן should then count fully by itself. Yet the תנא קמא and אחרים treat it as half a מתיר and argue about it.

steps.title: רבא: the knife makes the blood holy
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the blood is not holy while it is still in the animal's neck. The knife makes it holy, and making holy counts like permitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think the blood is already holy while it is in the animal's neck? No, the knife makes the blood holy, and something that comes to make holy is treated like something that comes to permit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב שימי. He shows that the slaughter of the פסח really does make something holy: the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי assumed the slaughter makes nothing holy. רבא says the blood only becomes holy through the cut of the knife. So the slaughter is a holy-making step, which counts like a מתיר, and cutting one סימן is really half of a מתיר. This fits his answer about the lambs in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal's neck
The knife makes it holy
Something that comes to make holy is treated like something that comes to permit

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, making something holy counts like permitting. The lambs make the loaves holy, and the knife makes the blood holy, so each counts as part of a מתיר.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
that the blood in the animal's neck is holy?
The blood — the knife makes it holy,
and something that comes to make holy
is like something that comes to permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מִי סָבְרַתְּ דָּם בְּצַוַּאר בְּהֵמָה קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slaughter of the פסח makes nothing holy, so the argument there cannot depend on making holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The knife makes the blood holy, so the slaughter is a holy-making step and counts like a מתיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא about intent during removal, placement and conveying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing when intent about the קומץ causes פיגול. It suggests that the conveying there means the walk to the altar for burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When is this said? During the removal of the handful, during placing it in a vessel, and during the conveying. Is it not talking about the conveying for burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a proof from a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists the steps of a מנחה where intent about the handful makes it פיגול, and the גמרא suggests that "conveying" means bringing it to the altar to be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof for the question in step 12. If "conveying" means the walk to the altar to burn it, then intent about the handful alone at that stage causes פיגול. That would support רבי יוחנן (carrying is like scooping) against ריש לקיש (carrying is like burning). The proof depends completely on which "conveying" the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (limits a rule to certain cases)
Removing a handful from the מנחה
Placing the handful into a holy service vessel
Conveying, carrying it to its next place
Burning on the altar

phrases.english: Come and hear:
When is this said?
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule that intent about the handful alone makes the מנחה פיגול.

phrases.english: During the removal of the handful, during the placement in a vessel, and during the conveying.
Is it not the conveying for burning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion with אביי and רב שימי, the גמרא returns to the dispute of step 13. It brings a ברייתא that seems to support רבי יוחנן against ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that intent about the handful alone during the walk to the altar causes פיגול (against ריש לקיש)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing קמיצה, מתן כלי and הילוך

steps.title: No, it means conveying to the vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא means the conveying that leads to placing the handful in the vessel, not the conveying for burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the conveying for placing it in the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof. It reads "conveying" as carrying the handful to the service vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means the conveying before the vessel, it says nothing about the walk to the altar for burning. So the proof from Step 22 falls away, and ריש לקיש's view still stands. The challenges that follow all test this reading on his behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: The conveying that comes before placing it in the vessel

phrases.english: No, the conveying for placement in the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading behind the proof in Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading of "conveying" in the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed "conveying" means the walk to burn it. It can mean the conveying to the vessel instead.

steps.title: Then the order of the list is wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the conveying comes before the vessel, why does the ברייתא list placement in the vessel first and conveying after it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say "placement in a vessel and conveying"? It should have said "conveying and placement in a vessel"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from Step 23. It uses the order of the words in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the steps in order: removal, vessel, conveying. That order suggests the conveying comes after the vessel, which would be the walk for burning. If it meant the conveying before the vessel, it should have listed conveying first.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It should have said

phrases.english: If so,
why "during the placement in a vessel and during the conveying"?
It should have said "during the conveying and during the placement in a vessel"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the conveying is the one before the vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the steps in order and puts conveying after the vessel, so it seems to mean the conveying for burning.

steps.title: Teach the ברייתא in the other order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is not difficult: teach the ברייתא with conveying before placement in the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult; teach it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the order by fixing the wording of the ברייתא. It puts conveying before placement in the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the order is switched, the list matches the reading from Step 23. So the ברייתא is not about the walk for burning, and the proof from Step 22 stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never said the conveying for burning causes פיגול. That was only the suggested reading, and it has now been pushed away.

phrases.english: This is not difficult;
teach it this way.
phrases.notes: He means: switch the order in the ברייתא, so it reads "conveying" and then "placement in a vessel".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about word order in Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of the list shows the conveying comes after the vessel, so it is the walk for burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should be taught with conveying first, so it means the conveying before the vessel, and the proof fails.

steps.title: Why Does the ברייתא Say 'Burning' Instead of 'Conveying'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'once he comes to the הקטרה.' According to the reading of step 23, it should have said 'once he comes to the הולכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says 'he came to the burning'? It should have said 'he came to the conveying'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 23 using the next line of the same ברייתא. If the ברייתא's earlier 'conveying' happened before the vessel, there is still a walk to the altar left, so the ברייתא should mention it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said the ברייתא's הולכה is the walk before the קומץ goes into the vessel. If so, a second walk, to the altar, still comes after the vessel. The ברייתא jumps straight to הקטרה and skips that walk, which looks like a gap in the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the קומץ on the altar
Conveying, carrying the offering to its place
It should have said

phrases.english: He came to the burning?
It should have said: he came to the conveying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the order of the ברייתא's list in step 25, the גמרא challenges the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא's הולכה comes before the vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the walk to the altar still remains, the ברייתא should say 'conveying,' not 'burning.'

steps.title: The Walk to the Altar Is Called Burning
steps.stepSummary: The walk to the altar serves the burning, so the ברייתא calls it הקטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Since this conveying is for the sake of the burning, the ברייתא calls it burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא did include the walk to the altar. It just called that walk by the name of the burning it leads to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason to walk to the altar is to burn the קומץ there, so the walk can carry the burning's name. That means the ברייתא's word הקטרה covers both the walk and the burning, and the reading from step 23 survives.

keyTerms.meaning: A need, something done for the sake of
It calls it, it names it

phrases.english: This is not difficult;
since the conveying is for the need of the burning,
it calls it burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, כֵּיוָן דְּהוֹלָכָה צוֹרֶךְ דְּהַקְטָרָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word: הקטרה here includes the walk that serves it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's word 'burning' means only the burning itself, so the walk to the altar is missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Burning' includes the walk to the altar, since that walk is done for the sake of the burning.

steps.title: Why Does the ברייתא Say 'Placed' Instead of 'Carried'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes placing the קומץ in silence. According to step 23's reading, it should describe carrying it in silence.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'he placed the קומץ in silence.' It should have said 'he carried' it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from the ברייתא. In this line the stage is described as 'placing,' when according to step 23 it should be 'carrying.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: At this stage of the ברייתא the קומץ is put on the altar with no wrong intent ('in silence'). According to the reading from step 23, the action being done at this point is the walk to the altar. So the ברייתא should have said 'he carried,' not 'he placed.'

keyTerms.meaning: In silence, with no special intent
He carried, he conveyed

phrases.english: But: 'he placed the handful in silence'
phrases.notes: 'In silence' means he had no wrong intent while doing this. The ברייתא goes on to say the wrong intent came with the לבונה.

phrases.english: It should have said 'he carried'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, נָתַן אֶת הַקּוֹמֶץ בִּשְׁתִיקָה – הוֹלִיךְ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new wording challenge from the same ברייתא, after the answer in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא's הולכה comes before the vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this reading the stage being described is the walk, so the ברייתא should use the word 'carried,' not 'placed.'

steps.title: The Difficulty Stays Unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the last challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the question open and does not offer an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the challenge stands with no answer. It is weaker than תיובתא, which would fully knock down the view. The reading from step 23 defends ריש לקיש's view. That reading, and with it ריש לקיש, is left with a problem, but it is not thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty left unanswered (not a full refutation)

steps.whatToRemember: The reading that the ברייתא's 'conveying' comes before the vessel answers one wording problem (step 27). It is left with one open difficulty: the word 'placed.'
steps.confusionAlert: קשיא at the end means 'this remains a problem.' It does not mean the view has been rejected, the way תיובתא would.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes step 28 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge from 'he placed' remains an unanswered difficulty.

steps.title: Burning the קומץ One Sesame Seed at a Time: Three Opinions
steps.stepSummary: Someone burned the קומץ in tiny amounts, each with intent to eat a tiny amount the next day. Three אמוראים disagree: פיגול, פסול, or כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He burned a sesame-seed amount with intent to eat a sesame-seed amount, until the whole קומץ was used up. רב חסדא, רב המנונא and רב ששת disagree: one says it is פיגול, one says it is פסול, and one says it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case and records a three-way dispute between אמוראים. The case is a wrong intent spread out in tiny pieces over the whole burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single burning carried the intent to eat a full amount (כזית) the next day. Each burning was a sesame seed with intent for a sesame seed. The question is whether these tiny intents add up. One view says they add up to full פיגול. One says the offering is only disqualified. One says it stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A sesame seed, a tiny amount
An offering ruined by intent to eat it after its time; eating it brings כרת
Disqualified, but without the כרת of פיגול
Valid, fit

phrases.english: He burned a sesame seed, intending to eat a sesame seed,
phrases.notes: He burns a tiny bit of the קומץ while planning to eat a tiny bit of the rest of the מנחה the next day.

phrases.english: until the entire handful was used up:

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda, Rav Hamnuna and Rav Sheshet:
one says: piggul;
and one says: disqualified;
and one says: fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about intent of פיגול during part of the service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-way dispute over tiny intents spread across the whole burning: פיגול, פסול, or כשר.

steps.title: Suggesting That Each View Follows a Different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the פיגול view follows רבי מאיר, the פסול view follows the רבנן, and the כשר view follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say: the one who says פיגול follows רבי מאיר, the one who says פסול follows the רבנן, and the one who says כשר follows רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that each of the three אמוראים is just following an earlier תנאי dispute. This is a suggestion, and it sets up the next move, where the גמרא will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that intent during part of the service is enough for פיגול. The רבנן say such intent only disqualifies. רבי holds (on 14a) that two half-amounts of intent do not join together, which could explain the view that it stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion the גמרא often goes on to question
The one who says

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא: מַאן דְּאָמַר פִּיגּוּל – כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Shall we say: the one who says piggul is like Rabbi Meir,
and the one who says disqualified is like the Rabbis,
and the one who says fit is like Rabbi?
phrases.notes: Back on 14a, רבי said two half-amounts of intent from two different acts don't add up to פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא: מַאן דְּאָמַר פִּיגּוּל – כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the three views of step 30 as following three earlier תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the three-way dispute among the אמוראים simply follows the earlier dispute among תנאים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's case may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the פיגול view must follow רבי מאיר. Perhaps רבי מאיר says פיגול only where the person intended a full measure, and here he intended only tiny amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Perhaps רבי מאיר only says it is פיגול there, where the person intended about a full measure. But here, where he did not intend a full measure, maybe רבי מאיר would not say פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to take apart the suggestion from step 31, starting with רבי מאיר. It argues that רבי מאיר's ruling may not apply to our case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's case, the wrong intent was about a full amount of eating. In our case, each intent was only about a tiny amount. So even רבי מאיר, who makes it פיגול quite easily, might not call this פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know? (a challenge to an assumption)
Perhaps
He only said his ruling up to here (meaning: only in that case)
He had in mind, he intended
The required measure, the full amount that counts

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי מאיר disagrees with the פיגול view. It is only saying we cannot prove that the פיגול view depends on him.

phrases.english: From where do you know this? Perhaps

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only says his ruling there
phrases.notes: "There" means the earlier case where רבי מאיר makes an offering פיגול even with wrong intent during only part of the service that permits it.

phrases.english: where he had in mind its full measure,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלֹא חִישֵּׁב בְּשִׁיעוּרוֹ – לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where he did not have in mind its full measure, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first part of step 31's suggestion, the link between the פיגול view and רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the פיגול view must follow רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר's case had intent for a full measure. Ours had only tiny amounts, so his ruling may not carry over.

steps.title: The רבנן's case may be different
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the רבנן say it is not פיגול only where the wrong intent covered part of the מתיר. Here it covered the whole מתיר, so even they might say פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps the רבנן only say there that it is not פיגול because he did not have the intent during the whole מתיר. But here he had the intent during the whole מתיר, so they too would say it is פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the rejection and now shows that the רבנן need not hold פסול in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן require the wrong intent to cover the entire מתיר, meaning both the קומץ and the לבונה. Here he burned everything bit by bit with intent each time, so the whole מתיר was covered. So the רבנן could agree it is פיגול, which means the פסול view does not have to follow them.

keyTerms.meaning: The part of the offering whose service permits the rest (here the קומץ and the לבונה)
Indeed, so too
He made it פיגול

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: And the Rabbis only say their ruling there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּלָא חַשֵּׁב בֵּיהּ בְּכוּלֵּיהּ מַתִּיר,
phrases.english: where he did not have the intent during the whole permitting part,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּחַשֵּׁב בֵּיהּ בְּכוּלֵּיהּ מַתִּיר –
phrases.english: but here, where he had the intent during the whole permitting part,
indeed he has made it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rejection of step 31, now for the link between the פסול view and the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the פסול view must follow the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן's reason (intent during only part of the מתיר) is missing here, so they may say פיגול.

steps.title: רבי's case may be different
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps רבי says כשר only where the half-amounts were not completed within the same service. Here everything was completed within one service, the burning, so even רבי might say פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps רבי only says it is כשר there because he did not complete the full amount from that same service. But here he did complete it from that same service, so he too would say it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last part of the rejection. The גמרא shows that רבי need not hold כשר in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי's case the small intents came from separate services, so they did not add up. Here all the tiny intents happened during one service, the burning, so they may add up to a full amount. That means the כשר view does not have to follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and filled it up, he completed the amount
A service in the Temple (slaughtering, burning, and so on)
He disqualified it

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabbi only says his ruling there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּלָא הֲדַר מַלְּיֵיהּ מֵאוֹתָהּ עֲבוֹדָה,
phrases.english: where he did not go back and complete it from that same service,
phrases.notes: In רבי's case each half-amount of intent came from a separate action, so they never joined into one full amount.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דַּהֲדַר מַלְּיֵיהּ מֵאוֹתָהּ עֲבוֹדָה –
phrases.english: but here, where he went back and completed it from that same service,
indeed he has disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes rejecting step 31, now for the link between the כשר view and רבי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the כשר view must follow רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In רבי's case the intents were not completed within one service. Here they were, so רבי may say פסול.

steps.title: Each view can be held by everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the three אמוראים are not following three different תנאים. Each one can say his view is accepted by all the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the one who says פיגול says it is everyone's opinion. The one who says פסול says it is everyone's opinion. The one who says כשר says it is everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this discussion. It drops the idea from step 31 and says each אמורא's view fits all the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each תנא's ruling can be limited to his own case (steps 32-34), our case is a new question. The אמוראים are arguing about it on their own, not repeating an older argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (a certain opinion)
Everyone's opinion, agreed on by all

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about burning the קומץ in tiny amounts is a fresh argument among the אמוראים. It does not depend on the argument between רבי מאיר, the רבנן and רבי, because each of their cases can be told apart from ours.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: before tying a later argument to an earlier one, it checks whether the earlier cases are really the same.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מַאן דְּאָמַר פִּיגּוּל – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: Rather, the one who says פיגול holds it is everyone's opinion,
the one who says disqualified holds it is everyone's opinion,
and the one who says fit holds it is everyone's opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מַאן דְּאָמַר פִּיגּוּל – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the three rejections in steps 32-34.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three views in step 30 are not tied to any תנאים. Each אמורא holds that all the תנאים agree with him.

steps.title: The reasoning of the view that says it is פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The one who says all agree it is פיגול holds that eating in small portions counts as eating, and burning in small portions counts as burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says everyone agrees it is פיגול holds that this is a normal way of eating, and also a normal way of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the first אמורא can say everyone agrees the מנחה is פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For פיגול you need two things: a real burning of the מתיר, and a wrong intent about a real act of eating. This view holds that small portions count both as burning and as eating. So the burning was valid, the wrong intent was about real eating, and the result is פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A normal way of eating, one that counts as eating
A normal way of burning on the מזבח, one that counts as burning
In this way (in small portions)
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: The one who says that all agree it is פיגול
holds: this is a normal way of eating,
phrases.notes: 'This way' means in tiny portions, the sesame-seed amounts from the case in step 30.

phrases.english: and this is a normal way of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאן דאמר פיגול דברי הכל קסבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind step 35's conclusion for the first view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating and burning in small portions both count, so the intent makes the מנחה פיגול according to everyone.

steps.title: The reasoning of the view that says it is פסול
steps.stepSummary: The one who says all agree it is פסול holds that small portions count neither as eating nor as burning, so the מנחה is like one whose קומץ was never burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says everyone agrees it is פסול holds that this is not a normal way of eating and not a normal way of burning. So it is like a מנחה that was never burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second אמורא can say everyone agrees the מנחה is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since tiny portions do not count as eating, the wrong intent was not about real eating, so there is no פיגול. But tiny portions also do not count as burning, so the קומץ was never properly offered. A מנחה whose קומץ was not burned is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified, but not פיגול (no כרת for eating it)
A מנחה whose קומץ was not burned

steps.confusionAlert: פסול here does not come from the wrong intent. It comes from the burning not counting. The intent itself does nothing.

phrases.english: And the one who says that all agree it is disqualified
holds: this is not a normal way of eating,
and this is not a normal way of burning,
and so it is like a meal offering that was not burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומאן דאמר פסול דברי הכל קסבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the second view, the opposite of step 36 on both points.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither eating nor burning in small portions counts, so there is no פיגול, but the מנחה is פסול because it was not properly burned.

steps.title: The reasoning of the view that says it is כשר
steps.stepSummary: The one who says all agree it is כשר holds that small portions count as burning but not as eating, so the burning was valid and the wrong intent means nothing. The word אמרי opens the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says everyone agrees it is כשר holds that this is a normal way of burning, but not a normal way of eating. Say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes with the third view, explaining why it can say everyone agrees the מנחה is כשר. The last word, אמרי, sets up the next part of the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning in small portions counts, so the קומץ was properly offered. But eating in small portions does not count as eating, so the wrong intent about eating is meaningless. With a valid burning and no meaningful intent, the מנחה is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid, fit

steps.whatToRemember: All three views can match all the תנאים. The argument is only about whether small portions count as eating and as burning: both count means פיגול, neither counts means פסול, and burning counts but eating does not means כשר.

phrases.english: And the one who says that all agree it is fit
holds: this is a normal way of burning,
but this is not a normal way of eating.
Say

steps.triggerLanguage: ומאן דאמר כשר דברי הכל קסבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three explanations begun in step 36.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each אמורא's view rests on how he judges eating and burning in small portions, not on a dispute between תנאים.
